title: Split-traffic experiments for prefetching + dynamic batching autotune with automated rollback
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Run randomized split-traffic trials to evaluate a combined prefetch (prefix/KV prewarm) and dynamic batching autotuner. We need a framework that: 1) safely applies config changes to a subset of traffic, 2) collects economic + quality + SLA telemetry, 3) computes statistically valid deltas, and 4) supports automated rollback when quality or latency regressions exceed thresholds. This ticket builds the experiment harness, defines metric instrumentation and dashboards, and wires in a runtime safety-circuit to auto-revert variants that violate SLOs or unit-cost guardrails.
acceptance_criteria:
- Ability to deploy two runtime variants (control + prefetch+autotune) to split traffic at route granularity.
- Telemetry captures cost delta (tokens/kg, GPU-ms/token), latency p50/p95/p99, error-rate, and quality proxies (rerank score, hallucination rate estimate) per variant.
- Statistical pipeline computes cohort-level deltas and confidence intervals within 6 hours of traffic.
- Dashboard surfaces economic delta, latency, and quality with alert thresholds.
- Safety circuit auto-rolls variant back within 10 minutes of threshold breach and records reason in audit log.
- Integration tests for traffic split logic and rollback smoke tests pass in CI.
test_plan:
1) Synthetic traffic replay with 3 workload profiles (short chat, long-context completion, embeddings-heavy) using traffic-replay tool.
2) Run 72-hour sandbox experiment to validate batching dynamics.
3) Inject latency and noise to validate rollback triggers.
4) Compute offline power analysis for expected traffic volumes.
5) Manual review of quality signals for sample of 5000 responses.
6) End-to-end runbook executed by oncall to rehearse rollback and incident notes recorded to Confluence.
rollout_plan:
Phase A (Canary): 2% of traffic for 24h, analyze metrics.
Phase B (Ramp): 10% for 48h if no regressions.
Phase C (Expanded): 30% for 72h with continuous monitoring.
Safety gates: auto-revert on (a) >=15% relative increase in p95 latency sustained for 5m, (b) >=8% relative decrease in rerank score proxy for 30m, or (c) cost increase >12% without throughput gains.
Post-mortem: If auto-revert fires, run post-incident analysis and block reattempt until engineering sign-off.
metrics_definitions:
- cost_per_1k_tokens: USD equivalent compute+infra cost normalized per 1k model tokens.
- latency_p50/p95/p99: end-to-end request completion time excluding network egress.
- tokens_per_gpu_sec: effective throughput metric for variant.
- rerank_accuracy_proxy: normalized score from internal reranker used as a low-latency quality proxy.
- hallucination_rate_est: heuristic flag rate (contradiction + low-entity-confidence) per 1k responses.
- error_rate: 5xx or model-level failure rate.
- rollback_count: number of auto-rollbacks triggered by safety circuit.
- cohort_econ_delta: percent change in cost_per_1k_tokens between variant and control for each user cohort.
telemetry_queries:
-- BigQuery: cohort econ delta
SELECT variant, cohort, AVG(cost_per_1k_tokens) AS avg_cost, AVG(latency_p95) AS p95 FROM experiments.batched_prefetch WHERE run_id='ENG-70221-2026-02' GROUP BY variant, cohort;

-- ClickHouse: rollback trigger rate
SELECT variant, countIf(reason='p95_latency') AS p95_rollbacks FROM infra.events WHERE experiment='ENG-70221' GROUP BY variant;

-- Flux/Grafana: tokens per GPU-second timeseries (pseudo)
from(bucket: "telemetry") |> range(start: -1d) |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "gpu_metrics" and r.variant == "treatment") |> mean()
